Journal of Hydrological Modelling
Volume 41, Issue 3, pages 220-238
Received 14 January 2023; accepted 2 May 2023

Rainfall-runoff prediction in small ungauged catchments using regionalised
recession parameters

Priya Raghunathan, Aaron Whitfield, and Lucia Ferrari

Department of Civil Engineering and Environmental Science, University of Oklahoma,
Norman, Oklahoma, United States

Abstract
Predicting runoff in ungauged catchments remains a central problem in operational
hydrology. We evaluate whether recession parameters regionalised from 84 gauged
catchments transfer to small ungauged basins in the south-central United States. Using
a leave-one-out framework, we find that regionalised parameters reproduce observed
peak flows within 18% for catchments below 50 square kilometres, but degrade markedly
where karst features are present. A simple screening test based on baseflow index
identifies the affected catchments in advance, improving median Nash-Sutcliffe
efficiency from 0.44 to 0.71 across the transfer set. The approach requires no
additional instrumentation and can be applied with nationally available datasets.

Keywords: ungauged catchments, recession analysis, regionalisation, karst hydrology

1. Introduction

Operational flood forecasting in small catchments is routinely constrained by the
absence of streamflow records.
